cases.question: Which employee took the highest time-off hours in the last six months?
cases.answer: Employee E005 (Synthetic Employee 05) took the highest approved time-off hours in the last six months — 16.0 hours across 1 requested day, measured over 2026-04-26 to 2026-10-26. This counts approved time-off request hours (approved requests assumed taken as requested), not payroll-paid hours; results cover the request records you're authorized to access.

answer_tables.caption: Top employee by approved time-off hours, 2026-04-26 to 2026-10-26
answer_tables.sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT employee_code, sum(hours) AS approved_hours, uniqExact(toDate(request_date)) AS requested_days FROM dbpcm_warehouse.timeoff_requests WHERE status = 'Approved' AND event_type = 'Time Off Request' AND request_date >= CAST('2026-04-26' AS DATE) AND request_date < CAST('2026-10-26' AS DATE) GROUP BY employee_code), ranked AS (SELECT employee_code, approved_hours, requested_days, dense_rank() OVER (ORDER BY approved_hours DESC) AS hours_rank FROM totals) SELECT employee_code AS "Employee Code", approved_hours AS "Approved Time-Off Hours", requested_days AS "Requested Days", hours_rank AS "Rank" FROM ranked WHERE hours_rank <= 1 ORDER BY hours_rank, employee_code

cases.question: What is the average tenure for each department?
cases.answer:
Average tenure by home department, for the current workforce (Active and On Leave employees), measured from original hire date to today (2026-10-26):

Operations has the longest average service (~5.3 years), followed by Human Resources (~4.5) and Engineering (~3.5). Information Technology currently has no active or on-leave staff, so no average tenure applies there.

answer_tables.caption: Average tenure (years) by department — Active + On Leave employees
answer_tables.sql:
SELECT d.department_name AS `Department`,
       coalesce(t.`Employees`, 0) AS `Employees`,
       t.`Average Tenure (Years)`
FROM dbpcm_datawarehouse.department d
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT e.department_name AS department_name,
         count(*) AS `Employees`,
         avg(dateDiff('day', toDate(e.hire_date), toDate('2026-10-26')) / 365.25) AS `Average Tenure (Years)`
  FROM dbpcm_datawarehouse.employee e
  WHERE e.employee_status IN ('Active', 'On Leave')
    AND toDate(e.hire_date) > toDate('1900-01-01')
    AND toDate(e.hire_date) <= toDate('2026-10-26')
  GROUP BY e.department_name
) t ON t.department_name = d.department_name
ORDER BY `Department`

cases.question: How much gross pay did that employee receive in those six months?
cases.answer:
Employee E005 (Synthetic Employee 05) received $15,498.00 in gross pay (earnings-register amounts, before taxes, deductions and benefits) over the six months 2026-04-26 to 2026-10-26, measured by pay (check) date. That total is the sum of 1,722 earnings line items spread across 86 pay dates, so it reflects line-item detail rather than a count of paychecks.

Coverage caveat: this employee's available earnings records run only from pay date 2026-08-01 through 2026-10-25 (monthly: Aug $5,589.00, Sep $5,463.00, Oct $4,446.00). No earnings rows exist earlier in the window, so this is the total for the period payroll data actually covers, not a full six-month figure. Results cover the records you are authorized to access.

cases.question: Did that employee have any punch records in those six months?
cases.answer:
Yes — E005 (Synthetic Employee 05) has punch-pair records in the six months from 2026-04-26 to 2026-10-25: 2 matched punch pairs on 2 observed days (2026-09-01 and 2026-09-02), all from the synthetic source. Note that these pairs carry 0.00 paid hours and $0.00 earning amount.

Caveat: this employee is salaried, and salaried time-off approvals and automatic pay-period-end timesheets can generate punch records without the employee clocking in. So the presence of these two pairs does not establish that the employee actually clocked in or was physically present.

answer_tables.caption: Punch-pair summary for E005, 2026-04-26 to 2026-10-25
answer_tables.sql: SELECT CASE 'employee' WHEN 'employee' THEN employee_code WHEN 'department' THEN department_code WHEN 'day' THEN toString(punch_date) WHEN 'month' THEN SUBSTRING(toString(punch_date), 1, 7) WHEN 'hours_type' THEN hours_type ELSE 'Company' END AS "Group", count(*) AS "Pair Count", count(DISTINCT employee_code) AS "Employee Count", count(DISTINCT punch_date) AS "Observed Days", sum(earn_hours) AS "Paid Hours", sum(earn_amount) AS "Pair Earning Amount", min(punch_date) AS "First Observed Date", max(punch_date) AS "Last Observed Date" FROM dbpcm_warehouse.punch_pair FINAL WHERE punch_date >= toDate('2026-04-26') AND punch_date < toDate('2026-10-26') AND table_source = 'synthetic' AND employee_code = 'E005' AND TRUE AND TRUE AND TRUE AND TRUE AND TRUE GROUP BY CASE 'employee' WHEN 'employee' THEN employee_code WHEN 'department' THEN department_code WHEN 'day' THEN toString(punch_date) WHEN 'month' THEN SUBSTRING(toString(punch_date), 1, 7) WHEN 'hours_type' THEN hours_type ELSE 'Company' END ORDER BY "Group"

cases.question: Show gross payroll earnings by employee home department for September 2026. Include all employee statuses, use payroll EARN amounts and employee department names.
cases.answer:
Gross payroll earnings (EARN) for September 2026 by employee home department, all employee statuses included:


Payroll line items with a September 2026 pay date were grouped by the employee's home department (the department recorded in the employee directory). All 24 employees on the September payroll matched a department record, so no earnings fell into an unmatched bucket. These are finalized gross earnings — the EARN register only — not net pay or total employer cost.

answer_tables.caption: Gross payroll earnings by employee home department, September 2026 (pay date)
answer_tables.sql:
SELECT e.department_name AS `Home Department`,
       sum(CAST(p.amount AS Decimal(38,2))) AS `Gross Earnings`,
       sum(CAST(p.line_count AS BIGINT)) AS `Source Line Count`,
       uniqExact(p.employee_code) AS `Employee Count`
FROM (
  SELECT employee_code, sum(amount) AS amount, count(*) AS line_count
  FROM dbpcm_datawarehouse.payroll
  WHERE register_type = 'EARN'
    AND pay_date >= toDate('2026-09-01') AND pay_date < toDate('2026-10-01')
  GROUP BY employee_code
) p
LEFT JOIN dbpcm_datawarehouse.employee e ON p.employee_code = e.employee_code
GROUP BY e.department_name
ORDER BY `Home Department`
